fork.note: LOCAL-FIXTURE ONLY. This benchmark is executed with scripts/official/empty_rpc.py (empty chain state) — it is NOT a mainnet-fork replay. block_number is a non-zero placeholder (approx. Ethereum height on the incident date) required by the runner; no real on-chain state is read. The incident actually spanned Ethereum, BSC and Base; the fixture uses a representative source->dest pair.

contracts.note: Reconstructed minimal model in official/; no production addresses are asserted. The attacker's own contract became a whitelisted sourceAddress on FEG's SmartBridge.

root_cause_summary.vulnerable_pattern: FEGSmartBridge.receiveMessage enforced the trusted-source check only on the RELEASE op; the SET_TRUSTED op that extends the trusted-source whitelist had no sourceAddress check, so an attacker could whitelist their own (untrusted) source and then release the reserve.
root_cause_summary.verification_bypass: Wormhole faithfully delivered the attacker's true sourceAddress; FEG's handler acted on an untrusted source for the whitelist-extension path.
root_cause_summary.fix: Require trustedSource[sourceAddress] on the SET_TRUSTED op as well, so only an already-trusted endpoint can extend the whitelist.
root_cause_summary.not_wormhole: The Wormhole Foundation stated its contracts were unaffected; the defect was a logical error in FEG's relay/SmartBridge.

exploit_characteristics.style: spoofed cross-chain message (self-whitelist) + reserve release, no deposit
exploit_characteristics.notes: No flash loan. Loss reported ~$1.0M-$1.3M across sources; recorded as a range lower bound.
